chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Imran ibn al-Hajjaj al-Sabi'i, from Muhammad ibn Walid, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whoever commits a sin, and knows that Allah is watching over it, if He wills He punishes him, and if He wills He forgives him; He forgives him even if he does not seek forgiveness.'
ai.seo_question: Does Allah forgive sins without the sinner seeking forgiveness?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the profound mercy of Allah, noting that awareness of His watchfulness (*munaẓẓir*) can lead to forgiveness even without explicit supplication (*istighfar*). This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *tawbah* (repentance) as an internal state of consciousness rather than merely a ritualistic act, underscing that divine grace often precedes human effort.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Imran Bin Al Hajjaj Al Sabi’e, from Muhamad Bin Waleed, from Yunus, Bin Yawoub, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The one who commits a sin, so he knows that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has been Notified upon it. If He<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires to He<sup>azwj</sup> Punishes him, and if He<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires to, He<sup>azwj</sup> Forgives him. He<sup>azwj</sup> would Forgive him and even if he does not seek Forgiveness’.
en.sarwar: 5. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Imran ibn al- Hajjaj al-Subay’i (from Muhammad ibn Walid) from Yunus ibn Ya’qub who has said the following:

“I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘If one commits a sin and knows that Allah is aware of it. He punishes him if He so wills or forgives him if He so wills. In such case. He (Allah) forgives him even if he does not ask forgiveness.’”
